messages.author: dd360cc5d7395a7b
messages.subject: Cross-Validation problem
parts:
First time user here. Using SEMs to test for a mediation effect. I'm trying to reproduce the target variable so as to get a predicted value for a Brier score. But I'm calculating the latent variable incorrectly and I can't figure out why. I created an example for diagnosis below. What am I doing wrong here?


library(lavaan)


val_spec <- '
             latent =~ obs1 + -0.3*obs2
             mediator ~ 1*latent
             #target ~ 2*mediator + 3*latent + 10       
'

tester <- simulateData(val_spec, sample.nobs=100000, return.fit=TRUE, model.type="sem")


tester$lat <- tester$obs1 + -0.3*tester$obs2
tester$med <- 1*tester$lat
tester$tar <- 3.0*tester$lat + 2*tester$med + 10

hunter <- glm(formula= tester$mediator ~ tester$obs1 + tester$obs2, data=tester, family=gaussian)

coef(hunter)[2]/1
coef(hunter)[3]/-0.3

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Cross-Validation problem
parts:
On 11/08/2013 02:38 AM, Christian Tillich-Walker wrote:

> tester$lat <- tester$obs1 + -0.3*tester$obs2

This is the problem. The latent variable is not just a function of obs1
and obs2. It is in fact the other way around: obs1 and ob2 are a
function of the latent.

If you want to 'compute' the latent variable values, you need to compute
what is called 'factor scores' in the literature. The formulas can be
found eg in Appendix 11 of

www.statmodel.com/download/techappen.pdf

in particular eqs 225 and 226, since your indicators are continuous.

You can take a peek in the lav_predict.R source file to see how
caculations are done. Look for the function lav_predict_eta_normal().

Yves.
